review_candidates.title: National Trainer
review_candidates.description: We have a fantastic opportunity for a National Trainer to join our amazing training team within Redhill/Burgess Hill with national travel as required.  As a National or Regional Trainer and valued member of the Training Team, you will play a key role in developing and supporting our workforce across the business. You will be responsible for delivering high-quality induction, mandatory and accredited training programmes, ensuring colleagues have the knowledge, skills and confidence required to perform their roles safely and effectively. Working closely with operational teams, mentors and key stakeholders, you will provide expert guidance, coaching and support to both new and existing colleagues. The role will also involve supporting driver theory training, coaching and driving assessments where required. You will be responsible for maintaining compliance with company policies, industry standards and regulatory requirements, ensuring that Patient Transport Services (PTS), Community Services, Courier Services and SAFE colleagues receive and maintain the training required for their role. Closing date for applications - Wednesday 30th September  What benefits can you expect? Circa £30,000 per annum. Full time permanent. Life Assurance – providing colleagues and their family financial peace of mind and protection to the value of £5,000. 24/7 online/telephone GP Consultation and access to prescriptions. 2nd opinion medical support following diagnosis or where a colleague is on a treatment pathway. Cash-plan benefits, providing colleagues the option of protecting themselves in case of illness and recuperation, including dental, optical, chiropody. Access to mental health consultations. Access to physiotherapy consultations. Access to legal advice on domestic issues e.g. motoring offences, wills and probate, and personal injury. Financial guidance re retirement planning, tax savings and state benefits. Long Service Recognition Scheme – recognising colleagues for their continued service after 5 years and at 5-year intervals with an increase in annual leave. Values-based Internal Recognition Scheme with financial reward, which will lead to an annual recognition event. Refer a Friend recruitment incentive scheme with financial rewards . The EMED foundation, to provide support to colleagues and our local communities. Paid holiday entitlement. Pension Scheme. Blue Light Card. Uniform provided. EAP (Employee Assistance Programme) to support a range of health and wellbeing requirements. Flu vaccination ( through an internal campaign in Autumn/Winter). Key Responsibilities Training Delivery Deliver company inductions for new starters across all divisions within your designated region and, where required, support national training activities. Deliver annual refresher and mandatory training programmes across all service lines. Deliver accredited First Aid qualifications and other approved training courses. Conduct driver coaching, theory sessions and practical driving assessments. Support and motivate learners to achieve successful outcomes and progress within their roles. Coach, support and assess Part-Time Trainers to ensure consistency and quality of delivery. Coach, support and develop Mentors within the region to enhance local learning and development. Encourage continuous professional development and support learners in reaching their full potential. Compliance and Quality Assurance Monitor, maintain and report on training compliance within agreed timescales. Ensure training records are accurate, up to date and fully auditable. Work collaboratively with Operations, HR, Compliance, Fleet and other stakeholders to address training priorities, risks and organisational objectives. Ensure all training activity aligns with company standards, customer requirements and regulatory obligations. Programme Development and Implementation Identify emerging training needs arising from changes in legislation, industry guidance, contractual requirements or organisational priorities. Contribute to the development, review and maintenance of training materials, ensuring content remains current, compliant and fit for purpose. Support the continuous improvement of training programmes, learning resources and delivery methods. Ensure all training provision aligns with business expectations and the EMED Training Prospectus. Collaboration and Communication Work closely with the wider Training Team, Operational Teams and Compliance colleagues to ensure a standardised approach to learning and development. Build effective relationships with operational teams and stakeholders across the organisation. Communicate professionally and confidently at all levels, addressing training-related challenges and opportunities. Deliver agreed objectives and key performance indicators in line with company expectations. Administration and Data Management Maintain accurate and timely training records using company systems, including Bamboo and other learning management platforms. Record accredited learning outcomes with external awarding organisations, such as Qualsafe, where required. Generate and distribute training certificates and ensure completion records are accurately recorded and retained. Produce training reports and compliance data to support operational planning and workforce development. Travel and Flexibility Travel throughout the assigned region and, where required, nationally to support business needs and training delivery. Demonstrate flexibility in working locations and hours to meet operational and training demands. Represent the Training Team professionally and positively, acting as an ambassador for EMED Group values and standards. We Are Looking For Essential Criteria Demonstrable understanding of the Ambulance Care Assistant (ACA) role and associated responsibilities. Ability to act as a positive role model, promoting professionalism, safety, and high standards of patient care. Current First Aid qualification or equivalent clinical competency. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Commitment to supporting the development and wellbeing of colleagues. Desirable Criteria Level 3 Certificate in Assessing Vocational Achievement (CAVA) or equivalent, or willingness to work towards. Level 3 Award in Education and Training (AET). Level 4 Certificate in Education and Training (or equivalent), or willingness to work towards. Assessor qualification. Driver Instructor qualification, Approved Driving Instructor (ADI), RoSPA qualification, or equivalent. Mental Health First Aider qualification. Experience in coaching, mentoring, or supporting staff development. Experience delivering safeguarding training. Experience delivering health and safety training. Previous experience facilitating training, coaching, or competency assessments within an operational healthcare or ambulance environment. Our Values Collaborative – we work as one team with a shared purpose to meet the needs of our patients, passengers, colleagues, customers, communities, and the planet. Agile – We listen, learn and adapt to improve the business, each other, and ourselves. Reliable – We do what we say we will do, we take responsibility and we behave with integrity. Empowered – We are confident and committed to taking responsibility to deliver the highest quality service. About Us EMED Group is an established healthcare logistics provider that enables access to health and social care through our four specialist divisions. We are one of the largest health and care partners to the NHS with 4,000 colleagues across over 60 bases UK-wide. EMED Group is committed to pro-actively improving the wellbeing of our communities by providing access to vital health and social care services across the UK.

review_candidates.title: National Position: Programme Analyst, FP/RHCS,Malawi,NOB
review_candidates.description: Job Description The Position: The Programme Analyst, Family Planning/Reproductive Health Commodity Security (FP/RHCS) contributes to the effective delivery of UNFPA activities in the areas of Maternal Health and Family Planning (FP). Under the direct supervision of the Programme Specialist, SRH, the Programme Analyst, contributes to the effective management of UNFPA programmes in support of national efforts to strengthen RHCS within existing programmes on maternal health, family planning, STI control, cervical cancer, etc. How you can make a difference: UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person's potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies. In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction. UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results. Job Purpose: The Programme Analyst, FP/RHCS works closely with other staff in the UNFPA Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) unit to support reproductive health commodity security and national health supply-chain initiatives. Within agreed workplans and under the guidance of the Programme Specialist (SRH), s/he contributes to forecasting and quantification, supply and procurement planning, pipeline monitoring, logistics management information systems, inventory management, warehousing, distribution and last-mile availability of contraceptives, maternal health medicines and other reproductive health commodities. S/he analyses commodity and logistics data, identifies emerging supply risks and brings them to the attention of the supervisor and relevant partners for follow-up. The Programme Analyst also provides inputs to planning, monitoring, evaluation and reporting for family planning, maternal health and condom programming. S/he coordinates activities of related project staff and consultants, and ensures oversight of the work of Implementing Partners (IP) in close collaboration with operations staff, programme officers, and counterparts at the Regional Office and HQ as well as in other UN Organizations, technical staff in government ministries and civil society organizations to ensure successful implementation of UNFPA-supported programmes to enhance RHCS, including the management of supply chain systems. Working closely with the Ministry of Health, national supply-chain institutions, districts, implementing partners and development partners, s/he supports implementation, information-sharing and follow-up of agreed actions to strengthen reproductive health commodity security. Within the context of health-system strengthening and financing, the Programme Analyst, FP/RHCS analyses relevant trends and provides technical and programme inputs to the formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of RHCS activities. Under the guidance of the Programme Specialist (SRH), s/he contributes to advocacy, policy dialogue, resource-mobilization activities and partner capacity development; monitors assigned results and budgets; supports the work of consultants and implementing partners; and maintains collaborative working relationships with government, development partners, civil society and other UN organizations. S/he contributes as a member of the SRH unit and the wider Country Office programme team. You would be responsible for: The Programme Analyst, FP/RHCS will be responsible for: General Programming Contribute to analysis and research of the political, social and economic situation in the country and preparation of substantive inputs to United Nations programming processes (Common Country Assessment [CCA], United Nations Development Assistance Framework [UNDAF], Country Programme Development [CPD], Country Programme Action Plan [CPAP]) as they relate to FP/RHCS, including management supply chain systems. Help create and document knowledge about current and emerging trends and issues, by analyzing programmes, projects, strategies, approaches and ongoing experience for lessons learned, best practices, and shares with management for use in knowledge sharing and planning future strategies. Technical Expertise/Management Analyse relevant policy, social and economic developments affecting RHCS, family planning and maternal health, and prepare briefs and technical inputs for programme development, policy dialogue and technical-assistance activities. Contribute to the availability and use of technical information and the analysis and documentation of RHCS issues, drawing on logistics information, surveys, administrative data and other relevant sources. Identify technical-assistance and capacity-development needs and provide inputs on appropriate programme responses. Support the implementation and monitoring of condom programming, including analysis of condom availability and utilization, in consultation with relevant stakeholders and under the guidance of the Programme Specialist, SRH. Contribute to advocacy for RHCS and family planning and to the development of appropriate communication strategies and materials. Provide technical and analytical inputs to forecasting, quantification and supply planning for contraceptives, maternal health medicines and other reproductive health commodities. Undertake routine pipeline, stock-status and commodity-availability analysis to identify potential stock-outs, overstocks, expiries and other supply risks, and flag these for follow-up by the supervisor and relevant partners. Support the collection, quality and use of logistics data through the national Logistics Management Information System and related platforms, including maintaining assigned dashboards and preparing periodic reports. Collaborate with procurement, logistics and programme colleagues to track the ordering, shipment, receipt and distribution of UNFPA-supported commodities; support agreed activities related to inventory management, warehousing, last-mile availability and commodity accountability; and participate in relevant coordination and capacity-development activities. Ensure compliance to Programme Supplies Policy. Advocacy and Resource Mobilization and Funds Management Assist advocacy and resource mobilization efforts of Country Office by preparing relevant documentation (i.e. project summaries, conference papers, speeches, donor profiles, and participating in donor meetings and public information events). Develop factsheets, briefing materials, info graphics, and presentations for public information, advocacy and resource mobilization purposes. Prepare relevant proposals with RHCS components and share information about UNFPA tools for co-financing and funding. Build strong technical and programme multi-sectoral partnerships for advocacy for RHCS within the broader SRHR agenda through national institutions, networks, alliances and coalitions. Monitor and keep updates on existing and potential partnerships. Follow through and ensure that recommendations and action points agreed to are addressed. Prepare and manage relevant budgets; Monitor expenditures to ensure delivery is in line with approved budgets and to realize targeted delivery levels and deliver timely and accurate reporting of financial information. Manage assets that have been procured by the UNFPA and supplied to the implementing partners; ensuring that they are put to proper use. Represent UNFPA at key events where required, with regard to UNFPA’s mandate. General Support Stand-in for other team members on selected functions, as may be required. Carry out any other duties as may be required by UNFPA leadership. Qualifications and Experience: Education: Advanced university degree in supply-chain management, logistics, pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, public health, health systems management, health economics or another field directly relevant to reproductive health commodity security. An advanced university degree in another relevant field may be accepted when combined with recognized specialized training and demonstrated professional experience in health supply-chain management or RHCS. Knowledge and Experience: At least two years of progressively responsible professional experience in reproductive health commodity security, health supply-chain management, pharmaceutical or public-health logistics, or a closely related field. Demonstrated practical experience in at least two of the following areas: forecasting and supply planning; pipeline and stock-status monitoring; logistics information systems and commodity-data analysis; or inventory management, warehousing and distribution. Knowledge of public-sector health supply chains, including the roles of Ministry of Health, Central Medical Stores (warehouse), districts and service-delivery facilities. Experience supporting contraceptives, maternal health medicines or other essential health commodities is desirable. Relevant professional training in health supply-chain management, logistics or commodity security is desirable. Experience using digital logistics information systems or supply-chain analytical tools is an asset. Experience in programme/ project management including experience in large multi-sector programmes. Experience working with the Ministry of Health and Local Government (districts) is desirable. Field experience is an asset. Prior experience in the UN system is an asset. A thorough understanding of the UN system in general, and especially UNFPA’s mandate, its policies and operations and current development topics and political issues in Malawi will be an added advantage. Demonstrated ability to work in a team. Languages: Fluency in English (Both Verbal and Written); knowledge of other official UN languages is desirable. Required Competencies: Values: Exemplifying integrity, Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system, Embracing cultural diversity, Embracing change Core Competencies: Achieving results, Being accountable, Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen, Thinking analytically and strategically, Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships, Functional Competencies: Advocacy/Advancing a policy-oriented agenda, Leveraging the resources of national governments and partners/ building strategic alliances and partnerships, Internal and external communication and advocacy for results mobilisation, Delivering results-based programmes, Project Management, Managing financial processes, Proficiency in current office software applications. Compensation and Benefits: This position offers an attractive remuneration package including a competitive net salary plus health insurance and other benefits as applicable. UNFPA Work Environment: UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance.
